verdict.rationale: Pipecat Flows documents functions that interface with external systems and APIs during a conversation, and it auto-derives function metadata from signatures and docstrings. Its site also mentions handing off long-running tools to subagents, which hints at keeping the conversation flowing. Nothing in the evidence explicitly shows filler speech, async tool-result speaking, or other dead-air mitigation during tool calls. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of how tool results are spoken without dead air (e.g., interim/filler responses or async function execution), core LLM function-calling docs outside Flows, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, my agent can call external APIs and custom functions mid-conversation and speak the result without awkward dead air

citations.quote: Process data by interfacing with external systems and APIs
Flows auto-derives the function's metadata — name, description, parameter properties (with their descriptions), and which parameters are required — from the function's signature and docstring.
Hand off to subagents for long-running tools and complex tasks
